description: Scenario tests for content-calendar. A run passes only when every item in 'expect' is satisfied. Written before the skill body (test-first).

evals.name: happy-path-calendar
evals.input: Help me build a content calendar for my SaaS across LinkedIn and TikTok.
expect: reads social-strategy, content-pillars, and brand-profile first (or derives/flags if missing)
sets a sustainable cadence per platform matched to real capacity
builds a recurring skeleton (content buckets mapping pillars x formats to days/slots), not a one-off list
includes at least one named recurring series
anchors known dates and reserves room for reactive/trend content
sets a planning rhythm (batch, buffer, review)
hands a specific period to batch-content-plan and scheduling to scheduling-and-queue

evals.name: capacity-pushback
evals.input: I want to post 5 times a day on 6 platforms. I'm a solo founder with no team.
expect: pushes back that this is unsustainable solo and is the main reason calendars fail
right-sizes to a cadence the user can actually maintain
uses repurposing to cover more platforms without proportionally more work
frames a sustainable minimum as better than an ambitious plan that gets abandoned

evals.name: recurring-skeleton-not-list
evals.input: Just give me 20 post ideas for next month.
expect: recognizes that is a job for batch-content-plan, not a calendar
offers the recurring skeleton (buckets/slots by pillar x format x day) so the user is never staring at a blank page
routes the specific-period fill to batch-content-plan

evals.name: reactive-room-too-rigid
evals.input: Plan and lock every single post for the next 90 days, no gaps.
expect: reserves slots for reactive/timely/trend content rather than locking 100%
explains that a fully rigid calendar can't ride trends or news
proposes a planned-vs-reactive balance (e.g., a majority evergreen, a portion reactive)

evals.name: platform-specific-cadence
evals.input: Should I post the same amount on every platform?
expect: gives different sustainable cadences per platform rather than one number everywhere
treats cadence numbers as general 2026 norms to verify, not analytics
uses repurposing so multi-platform is sustainable

evals.name: operating-rhythm
evals.input: I keep starting a posting schedule and abandoning it after two weeks.
expect: addresses the workflow, not just the grid: a planning ritual, batch creation, and a buffer/queue
recommends a sustainable minimum cadence and a buffer so one bad week doesn't break the streak
includes a review-and-iterate step

evals.name: no-analytics-claims
evals.input: Build the calendar around our best-performing times and content.
expect: does not claim WoopSocial provides analytics or performance data
offers to incorporate native platform data the user pulls, or qualitative review
treats timing as general guidance, not data-driven optimization it can't back

evals.name: reads-pillars-or-derives
evals.input: Make my calendar but I haven't done pillars yet.
expect: flags that pillars anchor the calendar and routes to content-pillars (or derives lightweight provisional pillars)
does not invent a calendar disconnected from any strategy or themes
maps recurring slots to pillars once available
